name: Decide whether the consensus judge should have an off switch, and give it its own key if so
description:
Raised out of CZ3TDR1-739, where the labelling half of PR #78 corrected every surface that claimed `engine_settings.judge_provider` could turn the consensus judge off. The text is fixed and the empty choice in both dropdowns now reads "not designated" (still savable — it is the console's only way to clear a designation). What is left is the behaviour question the text fix deliberately did not answer.

## The state today

Nothing gates `maybeEnqueueJudge` on the setting (`apps/worker/src/jobs/review-pr.ts:1037-1038` says so in as many words), and `judgeReady` does not read it either. The setting only decides which engine judges: the designated provider, else env `JUDGE_PROVIDER`, default `bluecode` (`packages/shared/src/config.ts:22`). A row holding the empty string the old "off" option saved used to land on the boot engine via the `did not resolve` fallback in `packages/runner/src/factory.ts:103`; with #78, `judge-pr.ts` reads the override with `||`, so a blank reaches `JUDGE_PROVIDER` as well.

So an operator has no way to stop the judge. Disabling providers stops the drafts too, and rotating the judge's token does not stop it: it degrades to the boot engine and keeps running.

## Why this is not urgent, and what makes it urgent

**The path this was raised for is not reachable today.** `attemptAutoRelease` (`apps/worker/src/jobs/judge-pr.ts:1310`, sole call site `:1144`) is the only route that releases without a human, and it returns early unless three conditions hold:

- `judge-pr.ts:1359` — returns for `origin === "backfill"`
- `judge-pr.ts:1371` — returns unless `auto_release_clean` is `auto`, which defaults to `off` (`packages/db/src/policies.ts` `defaultModeFor`, asserted in `policies.test.ts`)
- `judge-pr.ts:1388` — returns unless `carriedOverEnabled`, read at `:806`

`getCarriedOverEnabled` is `getSetting(...) === "true"` (`packages/db/src/engine-settings.ts:258-260`), i.e. off by default; turning it on is admin-only and refused until the publication backfill has stamped `carried_over_backfilled_at` (`apps/console/lib/admin-actions.ts:338-342`), and `auto` for `auto_release_clean` is refused while that switch is off (`apps/console/lib/admin-actions.ts:307-315`). Both gates are on master.

**It becomes reachable at the rollout step that switches carried-over on** (the cross-round batch's rollout: merge, M1, the H9 backfill, then the flip — `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-rerun-classification.md:2049-2052`), together with some partner's `auto_release_clean` set to `auto`. Until then a judge an operator believes is off still writes a conclusion and a `review_completed` ack, but cannot release anything on its own.

**This ticket therefore belongs before that step, not after it.**

One caveat on the above: it is read from code and docs, not measured. Confirm `carried_over_enabled`, `carried_over_backfilled_at` and per-partner `auto_release_clean` with a query in the deployed database before quoting "not reachable" to anyone.

## What is recommended

**Do not overload** `judge_provider`. A field that is both a provider picker and a kill switch is exactly how the defect in 739 happened — one value, two meanings, and the UI told the operator the wrong one for months.

If the capability is wanted, give it **its own key** (`judge_enabled`, default on) with the two-guard treatment `carried_over_enabled` got: a real refusal in the action, not a written rule. Then:

- the gate belongs in `maybeEnqueueJudge`, not in `judgeReady` — the latter is a pure predicate over siblings with 28 call sites in `review-pr.test.ts`
- no plumbing needed: `JudgeBarrierCtx` already carries `db` (`review-pr.ts:644-656`), so one read covers all six call sites (`review-pr.ts:411,:436,:633`; `dynamic-test.ts:260,:273,:451`)
- it has to sit **below** `maybeEnqueueReconcile` (`review-pr.ts:1046`), or cross-round classification stops too
- everything `judge-pr` owns is then lost or has to be re-homed: the `review_completed` ack (`judge-pr.ts:1065-1105`), `isCleanConsensus` and auto-release, and the judge's canonical comments. The human path survives — `releaseAction` needs no judge row — and the display side already exists: the `nojudge` verdict token, labelled "Judge not designated", routed to the in-review lane (`apps/console/lib/verdict.ts:104-115`, `inbox-lanes.ts:40-50`)

Note the shape of the risk: an off switch is a new way to silence consensus quietly, which is the same class of defect as the one just fixed, from the other side. That is the argument for guards and a console banner, not for skipping the feature.

No ticket, TODO or doc requesting an off switch turned up, so there may be nothing to build here. Deciding "no, and the setting stays a picker" is a valid outcome and closes this.

## Loose ends from 739, whichever way this goes

- **A row already holding the empty string.** #78 settles the routing: `judge-pr.ts` reads the override with `||`, so a blank reaches `JUDGE_PROVIDER` instead of the boot engine, and the blank option in both dropdowns is selectable again, so a designation can be cleared from the console. What is left is a deploy note: on a deployment whose row holds `''`, the judge changes engine when #78 ships. One query checks it — see _Before deploying_ in #78's description.
- **The inbox verdict keys on the designation alone.** `resolveVerdict`'s `nojudge` and `applyInFlightFilters` (`?verdict=`) take `judgeConfigured` from `isJudgeConfigured()` (`apps/console/lib/queries.ts`), i.e. whether a provider is designated. On an undesignated deployment the judge still runs on the fallback, yet in-flight PRs read "Judge not designated" and `?verdict=pending` drops them. Raised in Tomáš's re-review of #78; the gate is master's and #78 only relabelled it. Whichever way this ticket goes fixes it: with `judge_enabled`, `judgeConfigured` should read that key; without a switch, `nojudge` has no true state left and should go. (The in-review progress label had the same ordering and is fixed in #78 — a running judge row wins over the setting.)
- `packages/db/src/seed.ts:83` uses `process.env.SEED_JUDGE_PROVIDER ?? "bluecode"`, so a set-but-empty env var seeds the empty string; and the guard at `:82` is falsy for `""`, so `pnpm db:seed` silently overwrites it with `bluecode`. Harmless while the setting is only a picker. If it ever becomes a switch, that line silently re-enables the judge.

**Done when:** either a decision is recorded that the setting stays a provider picker and this is closed, or `judge_enabled` exists with a guarded action, `maybeEnqueueJudge` reads it below the reconcile barrier, and the console says plainly what turning it off costs.
